newsitem.title: UK: London Stock Exchange unveils new listing rules.
newsitem.headline: London Stock Exchange unveils new listing rules.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange on Wednesday unveiled proposals for new listing rules which it said would help both companies wishing to join and investors.
The changes are aimed at reducing the burden on companies, eliminating outdated rules and ensuring the rules are readily understandable. One element would be to streamline the application process.

The LSE said it was seeking comment on the proposed changes to the rules, known as the "Yellow Book", and all responses would be displayed for two weeks after the end of the consultation period on June 20.

They include lifting current restrictions on the use of summary documents "to encourage the use of more user-friendly and more intelligible material for shareholders and to discourage the addition of unneccessary or excessive information".

The LSE said there would be greater flexibility in the use of pro-forma financial information. This would bring it in line with other regulators, particularly the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
It would also help increase investors' understanding of the basis of profit forecasts by lifting the current restriction on disclosure of the assumptions within the control of management.
The LSE is also proposing greater flexibility so a firm's directors or senior management "can provide a reasonable connection between the past and the future operation of the business".
But the rules would still specify that a company's board had sufficient relevant experience and expertise.
Duplication with Britain's Companies Act and other statutory requirements will be removed from the listing rules, particularly the contents of the annual report of accounts.
"In addition, changes are proposed to the rules on pre-emption rights to bring them into line with company law," the LSE said.
Rules relating to settlement will be deleted following the transfer of settlement from the exchange to CRESTCo.
In addition to the consultation document, the LSE said it had also published the new listing rule on the disclosure of directors' pensions.

This was effective for companies with a financial year end ending on or after July 1 and implements the recommendations made following the Greenbury Report. This is the last of the Greenbury recommendations to be included in the rules.
